headline: ACC probes corruption and money laundering against Asif Mahmud
summary: The former interim government adviser and NCP spokesperson denies the allegations, claiming the commission is being used as a tool.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has decided to investigate allegations of corruption, irregularities, abuse of power, and money laundering against Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain.
The ACC Assistant Director for Public Relations, Md Tanzir Ahmed, announced the decision during a regular media briefing today.
Asif Mahmud denied the allegations at a press conference in Dhaka’s Banglamotor, stating that the commission is being used for political purposes after a reform ordinance was scrapped.

The allegations include tender manipulation in city corporations, taking commissions from development projects under the Ministry of Local Government, and inflating project costs for rural infrastructure and bridge construction.

The complaint also alleges financial transactions related to recruitment and promotions at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, and bribery in the appointment of high-ranking officials at Dhaka WASA and LGED.

Furthermore, the ACC is probing claims that state funds were wasted on helicopter travel and that Asif Mahmud acquired assets in Portugal, Dubai, Singapore, Australia, and Switzerland through illicit earnings.
The investigation also covers allegations against his father, Bellal Hossain, and other personal staff, including alleged control over contractors' syndicates and bribery.
The ACC stated that the investigation is now underway and that all allegations raised in the complaint will be verified through the inquiry.
caption:
Corruption, money laundering, and assets in five countries. The ACC is now investigating former adviser Asif Mahmud.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has decided to investigate allegations of corruption, irregularities, abuse of power, and money laundering against Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain.

The ACC Assistant Director for Public Relations, Md Tanzir Ahmed, announced the decision during a regular media briefing today.

Asif Mahmud denied the allegations at a press conference in Dhaka’s Banglamotor, stating that the commission is being used for political purposes after a reform ordinance was scrapped.

The allegations include tender manipulation in city corporations, taking commissions from development projects under the Ministry of Local Government, and inflating project costs for rural infrastructure and bridge construction.

The complaint also alleges financial transactions related to recruitment and promotions at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, and bribery in the appointment of high-ranking officials at Dhaka WASA and LGED.

Furthermore, the ACC is probing claims that state funds were wasted on helicopter travel and that Asif Mahmud acquired assets in Portugal, Dubai, Singapore, Australia, and Switzerland through illicit earnings.

The investigation also covers allegations against his father, Bellal Hossain, and other personal staff, including alleged control over contractors' syndicates and bribery.

The ACC stated that the investigation is now underway and that all allegations raised in the complaint will be verified through the inquiry.

headline_marked: Rab arrests 5 for [[selling personal data from govt servers]]
headline: Rab arrests 5 for selling personal data from govt servers
summary: The suspects allegedly operated an encrypted website and used social media to trade confidential citizens' records, including NID and birth registration data.
details: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has arrested five individuals from across the country for allegedly selling citizens' personal information obtained from government servers.
One suspect, Abdus Salam Sarkar, reportedly launched an encrypted website called 'E Seba 24 Dot Top' in April to commercialize this data, allowing clients to purchase confidential files for money.
The compromised information included National Identity Card (NID) and birth registration records, call detail records (CDRs), mobile banking logs, SIM ownership profiles, and real-time location data.
The other four suspects allegedly used Facebook and WhatsApp to promote their services and take orders, routing payments through mobile banking accounts registered under fake identities.
According to Rab-2 Commander Additional DIG Naimul Hasan, the suspects provided accurate information because they were sourcing it directly from government servers.
The force is currently investigating who leaked the data from the state servers for cash, though they have found no involvement of law enforcement personnel so far.
Additional DIG Naimul Hasan noted that while law enforcement must follow strict legal processes to access surveillance data, the general public was somehow obtaining it illegally.
caption:
Your NID, birth certificate, and real-time location could have been for sale online. Rab has arrested 5 people for selling govt server data.

Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has arrested five individuals from across the country for allegedly selling citizens' personal information obtained from government servers.

One suspect, Abdus Salam Sarkar, reportedly launched an encrypted website called 'E Seba 24 Dot Top' in April to commercialize this data, allowing clients to purchase confidential files for money.

The compromised information included National Identity Card (NID) and birth registration records, call detail records (CDRs), mobile banking logs, SIM ownership profiles, and real-time location data.

The other four suspects allegedly used Facebook and WhatsApp to promote their services and take orders, routing payments through mobile banking accounts registered under fake identities.

According to Rab-2 Commander Additional DIG Naimul Hasan, the suspects provided accurate information because they were sourcing it directly from government servers.

The force is currently investigating who leaked the data from the state servers for cash, though they have found no involvement of law enforcement personnel so far.

Additional DIG Naimul Hasan noted that while law enforcement must follow strict legal processes to access surveillance data, the general public was somehow obtaining it illegally.
